name: Jezebel
bio: Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, whom Ahab, king of Israel, married — a union Scripture treats as the decisive turn of his reign toward unprecedented evil. Through this marriage Ahab began to serve and worship Baal himself, building a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria and making an Asherah pole, provoking the LORD to anger more than any king of Israel before him (1 Kings 16:31-33). After Elijah's prophets-of-Baal slaughter at Mount Carmel, Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, and she sent him a messenger with a death threat: "So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to morrow about this time." The threat worked — Elijah fled for his life all the way to Beersheba and then into the wilderness, eventually reaching Horeb (1 Kings 19:1-8). Jezebel's own active role in promoting Baal worship, her further clashes with Elijah, and her lasting infamy are told in detail in the chapters ahead.
